decisions.reason: The displayed sum correctly retains every observation, whereas the last sentence incorrectly attributes a distinct-input data convention to the natural-spline definition. Clarified that repeats affect residual weights but introduce no extra knots; AC, two distinct locations, lambda>0 and Sobolev evaluations are unchanged. The existence proof step 1.2 already groups all responses by location, and the one-input counterexample uses the unchanged criterion.

The dual identity is false when its denominator is zero (p=1 and xi_j=xi_{j+1} gives y-x=0). Source Theorem 5 explicitly requires a positive span. Repair step 2.1 applies it only for indices m-d+1 through m, whose spans contain the nonempty cell. Step 3.2 now derives the derivative formula using the local dual basis and positive spans, avoiding invalid zero-span cancellation. Truncated-power dimension, multiplicity smoothness, local independence and endpoint limits establish the unchanged full basis Statement.

At n=0 the stated n^{-1} training loss is undefined and the cited fixed-design definition requires n>=1. Added n,K>=1 and inputs in the basis domain. Also licensed the arbitrary supplied spline basis already required by the assigned risk theorem, preserving the canonical B-spline basis as an explicit special case. Projection onto the specified design remains unique at rank deficiency, and nearest-point comparison supplies coefficient minimizers without choosing a coefficient version.

The frozen estimator definition specified a B-spline basis while A3 and F1 use an arbitrary spline basis, leaving the identification unlicensed. The assigned supplier now accepts the very specified spline basis (retaining B-splines), and F1 explicitly binds the fit to it. The Statement is unchanged. Checked conditional product-kernel construction, Borel rank-stratified projection, trace<=K, exact orthogonal noise/bias split and integrable deterministic approximation. Also clarified that the first design pi-lambda extension fixes a response rectangle and declared the monotone-convergence supplier actually used for kernel countable additivity.

Closed adjacent neighborhoods overlap at an interior knot, contradicting the stated M=1 pointwise overlap condition. Replaced them with disjoint left-closed/right-open cells and included 1 in the final cell. For continuous inputs, endpoint values and the cell maximum are determined by interior limits, proving a.e. locality and L-infinity stability. Explicitly fixed p=l=1 and q=infinity; each point lies in one neighborhood. The two Peano-kernel integrals still have total absolute mass (x-u)(v-x)/2<=h^2/8, so the original sharp error calculation is unchanged.
